module_title: Storage and Generative AI Architectural Decisions
review_basis: All twenty numbered original Module 17 R2 WebP slides passed spatial audit; narration follows original slide order and on-screen teaching details rather than legacy lesson map.
part_title: Permission-Aware Retrieval, SQL Vectors, Graphs and S3 Vectors

scenes.title: AWS AI/Storage Architecture Decision: Kendra
scenes.narration: This architecture shows why permission-aware enterprise retrieval is more than keyword similarity. Sources such as SharePoint, S3, directory services and other enterprise systems contribute documents together with user and group access-control metadata. Amazon Kendra indexes content and the relevant ACL information. During a query, the application supplies a verified caller identity and retrieval filters must respect that user's effective permissions. The diagram then passes only authorized passages to the generative AI model, keeping inaccessible documents out of the context. Follow the four numbered stages: connectors, indexing, identity-aware retrieval and authorized generation. Do not trust user-provided group names from an unauthenticated request. Keep connector ACL synchronization and revocation behavior operationally sound, and verify that the generation pipeline cannot bypass retrieval filtering. This option is especially relevant for internal enterprise assistants where search quality and source permissions are equally important.

scenes.title: Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector
scenes.narration: This slide combines relational records, document embeddings and application metadata in Aurora PostgreSQL. The SQL example begins with a products table, filters a category and tenant identifier, then orders records by embedding distance from a query vector and limits the returned results. That example matters because vector similarity can operate alongside ordinary relational predicates and business joins. The pgvector extension adds vector data types and indexing methods on supported Aurora PostgreSQL versions. Index choices such as HNSW and IVF require tuning against real latency, recall and dataset sizes, and version support should be confirmed for your Region and engine. Enforce tenant isolation using trusted SQL predicates and appropriate database privileges or row-level security; a tenant filter in sample code alone is not a complete security boundary. Plan for storage, index maintenance, query concurrency, encryption, backups and operational recovery. Use this pattern when the application's relational data and embedding search belong together.

scenes.title: Neptune Analytics for Graph + Vector Retrieval
scenes.narration: The diagram moves beyond ordinary document retrieval by combining relationships with semantic similarity. First ingest enterprise data and extract entities and links, optionally generating vectors from relevant text or attributes. Neptune Analytics can then use graph traversal and vector similarity to find semantically related entities and expand through meaningful connections. The response stage passes relationship-grounded context to the AI application. This is different from simply retrieving the nearest text chunks. It is also different from the transactional Amazon Neptune database; Neptune Analytics is an analytics engine with its own supported graph and vector capabilities. The slide explicitly warns that ordinary document-only retrieval may be simpler with a vector store such as Aurora pgvector or OpenSearch Serverless. Verify availability, supported input formats, data-loading paths and query semantics for the intended Region and service version. This approach is valuable when relationships between people, products, research or events materially affect the answer.

scenes.title: Amazon S3 Vectors: Architecture and Tradeoffs
scenes.narration: Look at the separation between a regular S3 bucket containing source objects and an S3 vector bucket holding vector indexes with embeddings and metadata. An application embeds source documents, images or other supported content, then stores vectors with consistent dimensions and descriptive attributes. A query embedding retrieves nearest matches from an index, optionally constrained by metadata such as tenant, category, date or source. Keeping the same embedding model and distance configuration between ingestion and query helps preserve meaningful similarity results. The slide stresses two important trade-offs: latency, recall and operating cost depend on the index settings, data volume and actual query mix; S3 Vectors is not automatically the cheapest or fastest solution. IAM policies should restrict vector bucket creation, index changes, reads and searches, and tenant boundaries must not depend on trusting client-supplied metadata. Evaluate service limits and integrations such as Bedrock Knowledge Bases before choosing this design.
